push-zeros-to-back: Rearrange in place while keeping the relative order of the 'kept' items → read/write two pointers.
sorted-pair-hits-target: Sorted input + find a pair with a given sum → two pointers from both ends.
zero-sum-trios: Find all unique groups of three summing to a value → sort, fix one, two pointers for the rest.
three-flag-partition: Sort an array with only a few distinct values in place, in one pass → three-pointer partition.
widest-tank-between-walls: Pick two ends to maximise width × min height → two pointers moving the shorter side.
rain-pooled-in-skyline: Water level at each spot depends on the tallest bar on both sides → prefix/suffix max, or two pointers.
best-unique-window-sum: Fixed-length contiguous block + a condition on its contents → fixed-size sliding window with a count map.
longest-lit-streak: Longest run of consecutive equal values → one pass with a running counter (a window that resets).
streak-with-k-repairs: Longest contiguous stretch with 'at most k bad items' → variable sliding window counting bad items.
cheap-product-runs: Count subarrays with a monotone condition (positive values, product/sum below a cap) → sliding window adding window length per step.
two-bag-orchard-walk: Longest contiguous stretch with at most K distinct values → sliding window with a frequency map.
shortest-run-reaching-goal: Shortest contiguous run with sum ≥ target and all values positive → shrinking sliding window.
peak-in-every-frame: Max (or min) of every fixed-size window → monotonic deque.
exactly-k-kinds-runs: Count subarrays with EXACTLY k of something → atMost(k) − atMost(k−1) with sliding windows.
balance-point-index: Compare 'sum before i' with 'sum after i' → total sum plus a running prefix.
runs-hitting-exact-total: Count subarrays with an exact sum when values may be negative → prefix sum + hash map of counts.
neighbourhood-grid-totals: Many rectangle-sum queries on a fixed grid → 2D prefix sums with inclusion–exclusion.
product-of-the-others: 'Product of all except self' without division → prefix × suffix products.
run-divisible-by-k-len2: Subarray sum divisible by k → equal prefix-sum remainders; track earliest index for a length condition.
runs-divisible-count: Count subarrays whose sum is divisible by k → frequency of prefix-sum remainders.
best-profit-stretch: Maximum sum of a contiguous stretch → Kadane's algorithm.
biggest-multiplied-run: Max product subarray (negatives flip signs) → Kadane tracking both max and min.
ring-best-stretch: Max subarray sum on a circular array → max(Kadane max, total − Kadane min).
largest-swing-stretch: Max |sum| over subarrays → Kadane for max and min, or max prefix − min prefix.
mirror-letters-in-place: Reverse or mirror in place with O(1) memory → two pointers from both ends swapping.
phrase-reads-both-ways: Palindrome check while ignoring some characters → two pointers that skip and compare.
palindrome-with-one-eraser: Palindrome check allowing one deletion → two pointers, branch once at the first mismatch.
longest-mirror-segment: Longest palindromic substring → expand around every centre (odd and even).
count-mirror-segments: Count all palindromic substrings → expand around each centre and count steps.
scrambled-word-spots: Find all positions of an anagram/permutation inside a string → fixed-size window with letter counts.
longest-no-repeat-stretch: Longest substring with all-unique characters → sliding window with last-seen positions.
shuffled-code-inside: Does any substring permute into a given word? → fixed-size window with letter counts.
smallest-covering-window: Shortest substring containing all required characters (with counts) → expand/shrink window with a 'missing' counter.
glued-word-list-spots: Concatenation of equal-length words in any order → sliding window over word-sized chunks, one pass per offset.
winning-ballot-value: Element appearing more than n/2 times → Boyer–Moore voting (or a frequency map).
most-common-k-values: Top k by frequency → frequency map, then sort or heap by count.
letters-by-popularity: Order items by how often they appear → frequency count, then sort by count (bucket sort also works).
next-taller-lookup: 'First value to the right that is larger' → monotonic stack.
round-table-bigger: 'Next larger' on a circular array → monotonic stack over two passes with i % n.
days-until-warmer: 'How many days until a bigger value' → monotonic stack of indices.
price-streak-tracker: 'Consecutive previous days with value ≤ today', asked online one value at a time → monotonic stack of (value, count).
crashing-carts: Items moving in sequence where a new item can cancel several earlier ones → stack of survivors.
skyline-biggest-banner: 'Largest rectangle limited by the shortest bar in a range' → monotonic increasing stack.
solar-panel-block: Largest all-1 rectangle in a binary grid → row-by-row histogram + monotonic stack.
four-op-evaluator: Evaluate + − * / without parentheses, respecting precedence → stack of signed terms.
postfix-token-eval: Postfix (operator after its operands) expression → evaluate with a stack of values.
repeat-bracket-expand: Nested brackets where the inner part must be finished before the outer one → stack that saves the outer state.
plus-minus-brackets: Evaluate an expression with only + / - and nested parentheses, no eval → running sum plus a stack of saved (total, sign).
trim-digits-smallest: Delete k digits/characters to make the result as small as possible while keeping order → greedy monotonic stack.
one-of-each-letter: Keep each distinct letter once, preserve order, and get the lexicographically smallest result → greedy monotonic stack with last occurrences.
distinct-letter-pick: Subsequence with every distinct letter once, smallest in dictionary order → greedy monotonic stack with last positions.
drop-unpaired-brackets: Matching parentheses and deleting the ones without a partner → stack of open-bracket positions.
merge-biggest-digits: Pick k digits keeping relative order to form the largest number → monotonic stack per row, plus trying every split and a greedy merge.
locker-number-lookup: Sorted list + find one value + O(log n) asked → classic binary search.
whole-square-root: 'Largest integer such that a monotonic condition holds' → binary search on the answer range.
shelf-slot-finder: 'Index if found, otherwise where it would be inserted' in a sorted array → lower-bound binary search.
turned-dial-search: Sorted-then-rotated array + O(log n) search → binary search that checks which half is sorted.
turned-dial-smallest: Rotated sorted array + 'find the minimum / rotation point' in O(log n) → binary search against the right end.
summit-index: Values rise then fall (a single peak) + O(log n) → binary search on the slope (compare mid with mid + 1).
value-span-bounds: Sorted with duplicates + first/last position of a value → two boundary (lower-bound) binary searches.
staircase-grid-hunt: Grid sorted along rows AND columns → start from a corner where one direction grows and the other shrinks (staircase search).
snack-pace-minimum: 'Smallest speed/rate so that the job finishes within a limit' → binary search on the answer with a greedy check.
ferry-load-limit: Split an ordered list into at most D consecutive groups, minimise the largest group → binary search on the capacity + greedy count.
bus-relay-speed: 'Minimum integer speed so the total time stays within a limit' → binary search on the answer.
garden-bunch-wait: 'Earliest day/time at which a count-based condition becomes possible' → binary search on the day + greedy linear check.
spread-out-beacons: 'Maximise the minimum distance' when placing items → binary search on the answer with a greedy left-to-right check.
fair-chapter-split: Split an array into k consecutive parts and minimise the largest part sum → binary search on the answer + greedy.
bracket-balance-check: Matching pairs that must close in reverse order of opening → stack of open brackets.
patch-the-parens: Only one bracket type and you only need counts, not positions → a balance counter instead of a full stack.
nested-pair-points: Nested structure where an inner result must be combined with the outer one when the bracket closes → stack of partial results.
longest-closed-stretch: Longest contiguous valid bracket substring → stack of indices with a base sentinel (−1).
erase-key-typing: Typing with backspace / undo, compare final results → stack simulation (or backwards scan with a skip counter).
twin-letter-crush: Adjacent equal pairs disappear and the gap closes, causing chain reactions → stack of survivors.
case-pair-cancel: Neighbouring pairs cancel and the string closes up → stack of survivors.
snip-ab-cd: Delete fixed two-letter pairs repeatedly, with new pairs forming after deletions → stack simulation.
queue-from-two-piles: Build a FIFO structure from LIFO stacks → two stacks, pour one into the other lazily.
pile-from-a-line: Build a LIFO structure from a FIFO queue → rotate the queue after each push.
lowest-plate-stack: Stack that must answer min/max in O(1) → store the running minimum alongside each element.
capped-boost-stack: 'Add to the bottom k elements' on a stack with O(1) operations → lazy increment array pushed down on pop.
tick-tock: Produce something different depending on which numbers divide i → a loop with an ordered if / else-if chain on %.
richest-shop: "Each row's total, then the biggest" → row-wise accumulation with a running maximum.
halve-or-decrement: "Apply this step until you reach 0, count the steps" with halving → simulate; halving makes it logarithmic.
self-dividing-digits: "Look at each digit of a number" → peel digits with % 10 and / 10.
mirror-number: "Reads the same forwards and backwards" for a number → reverse its digits and compare.
add-one-digits: "A big number given as an array of digits, do arithmetic" → simulate school arithmetic with a carry from the right.
reverse-number: "Reverse the digits of a number" → rev = rev*10 + n%10, n /= 10.
digit-sum: "Something about each digit of a number" → loop with % 10 and / 10.
prime-check: "Is n prime" with n up to 10<sup>9</sup> → trial division up to √n.
gcd-lcm: "Greatest common divisor / least common multiple" → Euclid's gcd(b, a % b), then lcm = a / g * b.
running-sum: "The i-th value is the sum of everything up to i" → prefix sum with a running total.
even-length-numbers: "Something about how many digits each number has" → count digits by repeated / 10.
strip-value: "Remove a value in place and keep the order" → read pointer + write pointer.
dedupe-sorted: "Sorted array + remove duplicates in place" → compare with the last kept value, write pointer.
rotated-sorted-check: "Could this be a sorted array that was rotated" → count descents around the circle; at most one is allowed.
sorted-squares: "Sorted input with negatives, return sorted squares" → two pointers from both ends, fill from the back.
one-trade-profit: "Buy once, sell later, maximise profit" → running minimum and best difference in one pass.
rotate-right: "Rotate by k steps" with large k → reduce k mod n, then the three-reversal trick (or index math).
second-largest: "Second largest distinct value" → one pass tracking the top two.
move-zeros: "Move some elements to the end, keep the order of the rest, in place" → write pointer (stable partition).
pair-with-sum: Find two items that combine to a target, unsorted input → store what you have seen in a hash set and look up the complement.
any-repeat: "Does anything appear twice?" → remember what you have seen in a hash set.
same-letters: "Same letters, same counts, any order" → compare letter frequency counts.
cut-out-letters: "Can you build A from the pieces in B, each used once?" → count B's supply and spend it on A.
first-unique-char: "First element that appears exactly once" → count frequencies first, then scan in the original order.
common-values: "Values present in both lists, each once" → set lookup for membership, a set for uniqueness.
letter-families: "Group items that are the same up to rearrangement" → a canonical key (sorted letters) in a hash map.
longest-run-of-values: "Longest consecutive values, unsorted, aim for O(N)" → hash set plus counting only from run starts.
most-frequent: "Which value appears most often" → a frequency map, then pick the best entry.
merge-sorted: Two inputs that are already sorted and must be combined in order → two pointers, one per array (merge step).
line-up-mismatch: Compare the current order with the sorted order, and values come from a tiny range → sort a copy (or counting sort) and compare positions.
custom-order-sort: Order is defined by a second list and values are small → map value to rank (or count) and place in that order.
biggest-triangle: Choose items to maximise a sum under a pairwise inequality → sort, then the best candidates sit next to each other.
sort-array: Plain 'return the values in sorted order' with small n → any simple sort works; practise insertion sort, then use the built-in.
author-score: 'Largest h such that at least h items are ≥ h' → sort and compare each value with its rank.
kth-smallest: 'K-th smallest / largest' in an unsorted array → sort and index, or a size-k heap.
diagonal-sum: "Sum of the diagonals of a square grid" → index pattern [i][i] and [i][n−1−i], no nested loop needed.
transpose: "Row i of the answer is column i of the input" → swap the roles of the two indices.
refold-grid: "Refill in the same row-by-row order with a new shape" → treat the grid as a flat array and convert indices with / and %.
turn-grid-clockwise: "Rotate a square grid 90°, in place" → transpose + reverse each row.
spiral-order: "Return cells in clockwise spiral order" → layer-by-layer simulation with four shrinking boundaries.
zero-spread: "For every original zero, clear its row and column" → record first, modify later (two-pass with row/column markers).
sudoku-check: "No duplicates in any row, column or block" → one set (or boolean array) per group, check-then-mark.
sorted-grid-lookup: "Rows sorted and each row starts after the previous one ends" → the grid is one sorted array; binary search on the flat index.
grid-distance-to-nearest-zero: Distance from every cell to the nearest of many targets in an unweighted grid → multi-source BFS from all targets at once.
graph-copy-relabel-bfs: Copy a graph while relabelling nodes in discovery order → BFS with an old→new id map.
spreading-mould-minutes: Something spreads from several starting cells at the same speed and you need the time to cover everything → multi-source BFS counting layers.
king-moves-open-path: Fewest steps on a grid where every move costs the same → BFS (here with 8 neighbour directions).
one-letter-hops-chain: Shortest sequence of one-change transformations between two states → BFS where states are nodes.
paint-bucket-region: Change a connected region of same-valued cells starting from one cell → flood fill with DFS/BFS.
count-land-masses: Count groups of connected cells in a grid → scan + flood fill (connected components).
every-route-first-to-last: List all paths from a source to a target in a DAG → backtracking DFS with a current-path list.
nodes-that-always-halt: Nodes whose every path ends at a terminal (cannot reach a cycle) → reverse-graph topological peeling or 3-colour DFS.
friend-circle-count: 'Friends of friends are in the same group' and you count groups → connected components (DFS or union-find).
capture-enclosed-o: Regions that are 'enclosed' unless they touch the edge → flood fill from the border and flip whatever was not reached.
two-team-split-check: Split nodes into two groups so every edge crosses between them → bipartite check by 2-colouring.
largest-land-mass-area: Size of the biggest connected group of cells → flood fill each group and track the max count.
rain-reaches-both-coasts: Which cells can reach two different borders by a monotone rule → flood fill backwards from each border and intersect.
single-point-of-failure-links: 'Which single edge, if removed, disconnects the graph?' → bridges via Tarjan's low-link DFS.
can-finish-all-modules: Prerequisites between tasks and 'can all be done?' → cycle detection via topological sort (Kahn's).
smallest-module-order: Order tasks with prerequisites, preferring the smallest available each time → topological sort with a min-heap.
unknown-script-letter-order: Infer an ordering from pairwise 'comes before' clues in a sorted list → build edges then topological sort.
use-every-ticket-once: Use every edge exactly once in one walk (with a tie-break order) → Eulerian path via Hierholzer's algorithm.
extra-cable-in-tree: Edges added one by one and you need the one that first creates a cycle → union-find.
wire-all-posts-manhattan: Connect all points with minimum total cost → minimum spanning tree (Prim's for a dense/complete graph).
merge-contact-cards: Records that belong together if they share any item, possibly through a chain → union-find on the shared items.
signal-reach-all-time: Earliest arrival at every node with non-negative weighted edges from one source → Dijkstra.
cheapest-fare-limited-layovers: Cheapest path with a limit on the number of edges → Bellman–Ford for k+1 rounds (or BFS by levels).
flooding-pool-earliest-crossing: Minimise the worst (maximum) value along a path → Dijkstra with max instead of sum (a bottleneck path).
gentlest-hiking-route: Minimise the largest edge on a path through a grid → Dijkstra with max (or binary search + BFS).
quietest-town-within-range: Small number of nodes and you need distances between every pair → Floyd–Warshall.
fuse-booked-slots: Intervals in random order that must be combined when they overlap → sort by start and sweep, merging into the last block.
slot-in-new-booking: Insert one interval into an already sorted, non-overlapping list → linear scan: before / overlap / after.
fewest-cancelled-shows: Remove the fewest intervals so the rest don't overlap → keep the maximum set of non-overlapping intervals by earliest end.
fewest-laser-shots: Fewest points that stab every interval → sort by end and place each point at the earliest uncovered end.
stepping-stones-reach: Each element is a maximum jump length and you only ask 'can I reach the end?' → track the farthest reachable index greedily.
fewest-frog-hops: Minimum number of jumps where each value is a max jump length → BFS-style greedy over reachable windows.
shuttle-seat-check: Many ranges each adding a load, and you ask whether the total ever exceeds a limit → difference array / sweep line of +load at start and −load at end.
fewest-sprinklers: Cover a whole segment with the fewest given ranges → convert to 'farthest reach from each point' and run the minimum-jumps greedy.
cargo-van-items: Fixed-size slots and items of different values with no other constraint → sort by value and fill greedily.
happy-kids-snacks: Match two lists where an item satisfies a requirement if it is big enough, maximise matches → sort both and two-pointer greedy.
ticket-booth-change: Simulate a process where at each step one choice keeps strictly more options open → greedy simulation with counters.
biggest-glued-number: Arrange items so their concatenation is largest → sort with a pairwise 'a+b vs b+a' comparator.
split-unique-letter-chunks: Split a string so each character stays inside one part, as many parts as possible → last-occurrence map and extend-then-cut sweep.
next-arrangement: Next larger permutation in lexicographic order, in place → find the rightmost ascent, swap, reverse the suffix.
charging-loop-start: Circular route with gains and costs where the running total must stay non-negative → net-gain prefix sums (greedy reset or prefix minima).
fair-sticker-handout: Each element must beat its neighbours when it is larger, with the minimum total → two passes (left rule, right rule) and take the max.
toll-ladder-climb: Minimum cost to reach the end when each step goes 1 or 2 places forward → 1D DP over the last two states.
digit-letter-readings: Count the ways to split a string into valid 1- or 2-character pieces → 1D DP where each state adds the previous one or two.
ring-of-stalls: Pick non-adjacent items for max sum, and the items form a circle → run the linear house-robber DP twice, dropping the first or the last.
longest-rising-pick: Longest subsequence (keep order, skip allowed) that strictly increases → LIS: O(n²) DP or tails + binary search.
fewest-square-tiles: Minimum number of pieces from a fixed menu (squares, coins) to make a total, repeats allowed → unbounded coin-change style 1D DP.
robot-routes-with-walls: Count paths in a grid moving only right/down with blocked cells → 2D DP adding from top and left.
cheapest-grid-walk: Min-cost path from top-left to bottom-right moving right/down → grid DP taking min of top and left.
lightest-drop-path: Path from top row to bottom row moving to adjacent columns, minimise sum → row-by-row grid DP over the previous row.
cave-rescue-stamina: Minimum starting value so a running total never drops to 0 along a grid path → backward DP from the destination.
berry-field-round-trip: Go there and come back on a grid collecting items only once → model as two walkers moving together, DP over (step, row1, row2).
shared-letter-trail: Two strings + 'delete characters without reordering' + 'longest common' → a 2D DP over prefixes (the classic LCS table).
hidden-mirror-length: 'Delete characters so what remains reads the same both ways' on one string → interval DP on s[i..j] with matching ends.
typo-fix-count: 'Turn string A into string B with insert / delete / replace, minimum steps' → edit-distance DP over prefixes.
covering-string-length: 'Shortest string containing both as subsequences' → reduce to LCS: answer = n + m − LCS.
mirror-padding-inserts: 'Minimum insertions to make it a palindrome' → interval DP on matching ends, or n − LPS.
wildcard-star-pattern-match: Pattern with '.' (any char) and '*' (repeat previous) matched against the whole text → 2D DP on (text index, pattern index).
count-hidden-copies: 'In how many ways can word be picked out of text as a subsequence' → counting DP over prefixes (distinct subsequences).
fewest-mirror-cuts: 'Cut into pieces that are each palindromes, fewest cuts' → prefix DP where the last piece is a palindrome, found by expanding around centres.
fair-split-bags: 'Split items into two groups of equal sum' → subset sum to total/2, a 0/1 knapsack.
fewest-tokens-exact: 'Unlimited coins/tokens, pay an exact amount with the fewest' → unbounded knapsack DP on amount (coin change).
ways-to-pay-fare: 'Count the combinations (order doesn't matter) of unlimited coins that reach an amount' → counting knapsack with coins in the outer loop.
unlimited-trades-profit: 'Unlimited buy/sell, one share at a time, no fee' → state DP that reduces to summing every positive price change.
trades-with-rest-day: 'Trade as often as you like, but must wait a day after selling' → stock state machine with a cooldown state.
trades-with-broker-fee: 'Unlimited trades but each trade costs a fee' → hold/free stock DP subtracting the fee on sell.
two-round-trips-max: 'At most two buy-sell transactions' → stock DP with states for each transaction count.
k-round-trips-max: 'At most k transactions' → stock DP with buy[j]/sell[j] states for j = 1..k.
pop-the-lanterns: 'Remove items one by one, score depends on current neighbours' → interval DP choosing the LAST item removed in each range.
fuse-sand-piles: 'Merge exactly k adjacent groups, cost = their total, minimise to one group' → interval DP with prefix sums and a feasibility check.
cheapest-plank-sawing: 'Make all the cuts in any order, each cut costs the current piece length' → interval DP over sorted cut points.
tree-orchard-harvest: 'Pick nodes in a tree, no two adjacent (parent-child), maximise the sum' → tree DP returning (take, skip) from each subtree.
leaderboard-kth-score: A stream of values and 'k-th largest so far' asked again and again → a min-heap of size k.
boulder-crusher: 'Repeatedly take the two largest and put something back' → a max-heap simulation.
trending-tags: 'k most frequent' with a tie-break order → count with a map, then a size-k heap.
kth-biggest-value: 'k-th largest' in an unsorted array → a min-heap of size k (or quickselect).
cheapest-pair-totals: Two sorted lists and 'k smallest pair sums' → merge sorted rows with a min-heap.
running-middle-value: A stream of numbers with 'median so far' queries → two balanced heaps (max-heap low half, min-heap high half).
tightest-common-window: Several sorted lists and 'one element from every list' → a k-way min-heap with a running max.
cooldown-job-runner: 'Same item must wait n slots before repeating, minimize total time' → greedy on the most frequent item (heap or counting formula).
no-twin-neighbors: 'No two adjacent equal' plus 'rearrange' → frequency counts with a max-count feasibility rule (heap greedy, here made lexicographic).
moving-window-middles: 'Median of every window of size k' → two balanced halves (heaps or ordered sets) that support removal.
distinct-picks-with-repeats: 'Return all sub-collections' + 'may contain repeated values' + 'no duplicates' → sort, then backtrack and skip equal values at the same depth.
coin-combos-unlimited: 'Unlimited supply' + 'every different combination that sums to target' → backtrack with a start index that stays the same after picking.
coin-combos-single-use: 'Each coin used at most once' + 'values may repeat' + 'no duplicate combos' → sort, recurse at j+1, skip equal values at the same depth.
all-orderings: 'Return every ordering / arrangement of all elements' → permutation backtracking with a used[] array.
distinct-orderings: 'Every distinct ordering' + 'may contain duplicates' → sort, then permutation backtracking that skips an equal value whose left twin is unused.
bracket-builder: 'Generate every balanced/valid string of n pairs' → backtracking with open/close counters as the constraint.
mirror-word-cuts: 'Split a string into pieces where every piece satisfies a check, return all splits' → backtracking on the start index.
dotted-address-rebuild: 'Insert separators so every segment is valid, return all ways' with a fixed small number of segments → bounded backtracking with validity pruning.
fair-share-buckets: 'Split into k groups with equal sums', n ≤ 16 → backtracking over a bitmask of used items with memoization.
letter-trail-finder: 'Trace a word through adjacent grid cells without reusing a cell' → DFS with mark/unmark backtracking from every start cell.
treasure-cave-route: Small grid, 'never enter a cell twice', and you want the best path → try every path with backtracking DFS.
peaceful-queens-boards: 'Place items so that no two conflict' and 'return every arrangement' → constraint backtracking, one decision per row.
nine-by-nine-fill: Fill blanks so every row/column/group obeys a rule, with a unique valid completion → constraint backtracking with used-digit tables.
grid-word-hunt: Many words to find in one grid with up/down/left/right moves → trie of the words + backtracking DFS.
sweep-every-tile: Count paths that must visit every free cell exactly once on a tiny grid → backtracking DFS with a 'cells left' counter.
keypad-spellings: 'Every combination by choosing one option per position' → sequence-generating backtracking.
full-tree-blueprints: 'List every structure of size n' where a structure splits into two smaller ones → recursive generation with memo by size.
digit-sign-insertion: Insert operators between digits to hit a target, return all expressions → backtracking that tracks running value and last operand.
spaced-out-sentences: Split a string into dictionary words and return all the splits → backtracking over prefixes with memo on the suffix start.
rabbit-generations: Each answer is defined by the answers just before it (term = sum of the previous two) → linear recursion, made fast by memoizing or iterating.
hop-up-the-tower: Count the ways to reach a target where each move is one of a few fixed sizes → the count is the sum of the counts at the previous positions (linear recursion).
fast-exponent: A huge exponent and 'multiplying n times is too slow' → halve the problem each step (fast exponentiation, O(log n)).
robot-grid-routes: Count paths in a grid where you move only right or down → each cell's count = count from above + count from the left.
no-neighbor-picks: Pick items from a line to maximise a total, with a rule that no two neighbours can both be picked → take/skip recursion on the prefix.
recursive-chain-flip: A linked-list problem where 'the rest of the list' is a smaller copy of the same problem → recurse on head.next and fix up the head.
zip-sorted-chains: Two already-sorted sequences that must become one sorted sequence → merge by repeatedly taking the smaller front element.
every-selection: 'Return every possible selection / subset' → each element is in or out, so branch twice per element (2ⁿ results).
plus-minus-ways: Choose + or − for each number and count ways to hit a target → branch on each element, memoize on (index, running sum).
middle-of-two-sorted: Two sorted arrays and an O(log) target for an order statistic (median / k-th) → discard half of the candidates at every step.
chain-center-node: Find the middle of a linked list (you can't index it) → slow pointer 1 step, fast pointer 2 steps.
loop-in-the-trail: Detect whether following 'next' links ever repeats, with O(1) memory → Floyd's slow/fast pointers.
where-trails-merge: Two chains that may share a tail and you need the first shared node with O(1) memory → two pointers that swap starting points.
drop-kth-from-tail: 'k-th from the end' in a singly linked list, ideally in one pass → two pointers with a fixed gap of k.
loop-entry-marker: Find where a cycle starts using O(1) memory → Floyd: detect the meeting, then restart one pointer from the head.
odd-slots-then-even: Rearrange nodes by position into groups while keeping order, with O(1) space → build separate chains in one pass and join them.
build-your-own-chain: 'Implement a list with get/add/delete at an index' → nodes plus a sentinel head and a size counter.
mirror-chain-check: Palindrome check on a linked list with O(1) extra space → find the middle, reverse the second half, compare.
flip-a-stretch: Reverse only part of a linked list between two positions → anchor the node before the part and reverse in place.
partner-pair-max: Pair the i-th node from the front with the i-th from the back in a linked list → reverse the second half and walk both halves together.
swap-neighbors: Do the same small rearrangement on every consecutive pair of a list → solve the first pair, recurse on the rest.
spin-the-chain: Rotate a list by a possibly huge k → reduce k mod length, close the list into a ring, cut at the right place.
flip-in-blocks: Reverse a linked list in fixed-size chunks, leaving a short tail alone → check k ahead, reverse k in place, reconnect, move on.
squash-repeats: Remove duplicates from a sorted list → duplicates are adjacent, so compare each node with the next.
digit-chain-addition: Numbers too long for built-in types, stored digit by digit → simulate column addition with a carry.
chain-merge-sort: Sort a linked list in O(n log n) → merge sort, since lists split and merge cheaply but can't be indexed.
front-back-weave: Interleave nodes from the front and the back of a list → middle + reverse second half + merge alternately.
split-around-pivot: Stable partition of a linked list around a value → build two chains with dummy heads and join them.
clone-with-shortcuts: A copy where extra pointers can point anywhere, including forward → first map every old node to its new identity, then wire the extra pointers.
merge-many-chains: Merge k sorted sequences → keep the current front of each in a min-heap.
recent-use-cache: 'Evict the least recently used' with O(1) operations → hash map + doubly linked list.
flatten-layered-chain: A list where nodes can open a nested sub-list that must be expanded in place → depth-first (preorder) traversal.
frequency-evict-cache: 'Evict the least frequently used, break ties by least recent' in O(1) → per-count recency lists + a running minimum count.
tree-inorder-walk: "Left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree" → inorder depth-first traversal.
mirror-image-tree: "Folding the tree onto itself" → compare left and right subtrees as a mirrored pair with DFS.
longest-tree-route: "Longest path between any two nodes, not necessarily through the root" → post-order DFS returning height, update a global best.
height-balance-check: "Heights must differ by at most 1 at every node" → one post-order DFS returning height or a failure sentinel.
tree-height-count: "Number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path" → simple DFS combining the children's answers.
root-to-leaf-target: "Path from the root to a leaf with a given sum" → DFS passing the remaining target down.
embedded-subtree-match: "Some node with all its descendants equals another tree" → for each node, run a same-tree DFS.
all-target-routes: "List every root-to-leaf path with a property" → DFS with a shared path list and backtracking.
downward-segment-sums: "Count paths with a given sum that may start and end anywhere going downward" → prefix sums plus a hashmap during DFS.
complete-tree-size: "Complete (packed) tree, do better than visiting every node" → compare leftmost and rightmost depths to spot perfect subtrees.
nodes-k-steps-away: 'Move to a child or to the parent' + 'exactly k edges away' → add parent links and BFS the tree as a graph.
heaviest-tree-path: 'Path may start and end anywhere' + 'largest sum' in a tree → post-order DFS returning a one-sided gain while tracking the two-sided best.
tree-guard-placement: 'Minimum nodes to choose so every node is covered by itself, parent or child' → greedy post-order DFS with covered/needs/has-tower states.
level-mean-values: 'One value per depth / per floor' → level-order BFS with a size-per-level loop.
tree-rows-top-down: 'Group values by depth, left to right' → BFS with a queue, one loop iteration per level.
snake-level-walk: 'Row by row but alternate direction each level' → level-order BFS plus a direction flag.
rightmost-per-level: 'Only the rightmost node on each depth' → level-order BFS keeping the last node of each level.
column-sorted-tree: 'Group by column, top to bottom, ties by value' → record (col, row, val) for each node, sort, then group.
widest-level-span: 'Width counting empty spots as if the tree were complete' → heap-style position numbers in a level-order BFS.
mirror-flip-tree: When every node gets the same local change (swap the children), a simple recursive DFS over the tree does the job.
deepest-shared-ancestor: When you need the deepest node that has two given nodes below it, think of a lowest-common-ancestor DFS that passes results back up.
tree-to-right-chain: When you must restructure a tree in place into pre-order, think of linking each right subtree to the rightmost node of the left subtree, the same trick used in Morris traversal.
rebuild-from-pre-in: When you are given two traversal orders and asked to rebuild the tree, the root comes from preorder or postorder and the left/right split comes from inorder.
rebuild-from-in-post: When you get inorder plus postorder, the root is the last postorder value, and inorder splits the left and right subtrees.
kth-ancestor-jumps: When there are many 'go up k steps' queries on a fixed tree, binary lifting (a table of 2<sup>j</sup> jumps) is the usual tool.
tree-text-codec: When you need to turn a tree into text and back, think of a pre-order DFS with explicit null markers.
balanced-from-sorted: When a sorted array must become a balanced BST, pick the middle as the root and recurse on each half.
bst-find-subtree: When the tree is a binary search tree and you need to find a key, walk down one path, choosing left or right by comparing.
bst-add-leaf: Add a key to a BST without reshaping it → follow the search path and attach at the first null child.
bst-order-check: "All values in the left subtree smaller" → validate with an inherited (low, high) range, not just parent–child checks.
bst-remove-key: Delete from a BST while keeping order → recursive delete with the in-order successor for two-child nodes.
bst-kth-lowest: "k-th smallest" in a BST → in-order traversal gives sorted order; stop at step k.
bst-suffix-sum-rewrite: "Plus the sum of all values greater than it" in a BST → reverse in-order traversal with a running sum.
bst-ascending-walker: "Return keys one at a time in sorted order, using O(height) memory" → controlled in-order traversal with a stack.
bst-shared-ancestor: Common ancestor in a tree that is a BST → compare both keys with the current node and walk one path down.
bst-fix-swapped-pair: "Exactly two values swapped in a BST" → in-order should be sorted; find the out-of-order spots.
best-search-subtree-sum: "Largest sum among subtrees that are valid BSTs" → bottom-up DFS returning (isBST, min, max, sum).
prefix-tree-word-store: 'Insert words, then ask exact-match and begins-with questions' → store them in a trie (prefix tree).
wildcard-word-dictionary: 'Store words, then match patterns where a dot means any letter' → trie plus DFS that branches only on the wildcard.
shared-opening-letters: 'Longest beginning that all strings share' → compare characters column by column (or walk a trie of the words).
typeahead-top-three: 'Autocomplete: up to three alphabetically smallest matches per typed prefix' → sort + binary search (or a trie that stores top suggestions).
split-into-dictionary-words: 'Can the string be cut into pieces that all come from a word list?' → prefix DP (word break), with a trie to find matching words fast.
shorten-to-root: 'Replace each word by the shortest root it begins with' → trie of roots, stop at the first end-of-root mark.
words-built-from-words: 'Words that are concatenations of other words in the same list' → sort by length, then word break with a trie of shorter words.
xor-of-every-group: 'Sum of XOR over all subsets' with tiny n → enumerate subsets (bitmasks / recursion), or notice each bit is on in half of them.
best-xor-pair: 'Maximum XOR of two numbers from an array' → binary trie, go for the opposite bit from the top.
capped-xor-queries: 'Max XOR, but only with elements up to a limit, many queries' → offline sorting by the limit + incremental binary trie.
absent-from-range: 'n distinct numbers from 0..n, find the missing one' → XOR (or sum) everything that should be there against what is there.
count-lit-bits: 'How many 1s in the binary form' → bit tricks: n & (n − 1) removes one set bit per step.
is-doubling-number: 'Is n a power of two?' → exactly one set bit: n > 0 and n & (n − 1) == 0.
unpaired-value: 'Every value appears twice except one, O(1) space' → XOR everything.
odd-one-out-of-triples: 'Every value appears three times except one, constant space' → count each bit position modulo 3.
two-unpaired-values: 'Exactly two values appear once, the rest twice, O(1) space' → XOR all, then split by a set bit of the XOR.
range-xor-lookups: 'Many range queries asking for the XOR of a subarray' → prefix XOR, like prefix sums.
